title: Minimizing Power Waste in Heterogenous Computing via Adaptive Uncore Scaling
problem: In GPU-dominant heterogeneous systems, uncore (memory, cache, interconnect) frequencies remain at maximum because scaling only occurs when CPU power nears TDP—a rare event in GPU workloads, wasting power.
motivation: Uncore power is significant in HPC systems; GPU-dominant workloads don't stress CPUs, so traditional frequency scaling policies don't apply; dynamic phase-aware scaling could reclaim power without hurting performance.
method: MAGUS runtime monitors memory access patterns and predicts memory intensity. Detects execution phases and scales uncore frequency accordingly. Handles phase transitions smoothly. Integrates vendor power management features (e.g., NVIDIA DCGM, Intel RAS). User-transparent deployment.
key_novelty: First uncore scaling system aware of GPU-dominant workload phases; 27% energy savings while maintaining <5% performance loss.
contributions: Phase-aware uncore frequency scaling for GPU-dominant workloads
Real-time memory access monitoring and prediction
27% energy savings with <5% performance loss on heterogeneous systems
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific benchmarks; vendor-specific power interfaces may limit portability; phase detection heuristics may not generalize; actual energy measurements not detailed.
primary_theme: Adaptive power management for GPU-dominant HPC systems
